status.detail: Rider-specific window enumeration needs a focused process/owner identity trace.

next_action.label: Design fix
next_action.reason: Reproduce and capture Rider window identity before finalizing grouping.

judgment.rationale: The report is specific and current enough for maintainer reproduction. Current Window Hopper code groups candidates by the exact resolved process image path, so Rider windows split across host processes or represented by owned/tool windows are a plausible, testable cause.
evidence: PowerToys 0.101.2362 stable; multiple Rider windows; several tested shortcuts; Window Hopper works in other applications.
Current AltWindowCycle.cpp resolves the foreground process image and keeps only eligible windows with the same process key.
No duplicate, assignee, or linked implementation was found in the live issue timeline.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce with multiple Rider projects and inspect each top-level window process/owner before designing process-family grouping.

fix_assessment.rationale: No merged or active fix was found for the identified current code path; the focused plan should be validated before implementation.

proposed_fixes.title: Group Rider frames by application identity when exact process paths differ
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Window Hopper currently filters eligible windows by exact resolved process image path; Rider may expose project frames through different host processes or ownership relationships, leaving the same-process candidate set empty.
plan: Capture HWND, owner, process path, AppUserModelID, and eligibility for two Rider project windows.
Introduce a narrowly scoped application-identity/grouping key only where exact process identity is insufficient.
Add AltWindowCycleLogic tests for multiple eligible frames across a recognized application group while preserving process isolation for unrelated apps.
verification: Launch two Rider project windows and verify thumbnails appear and cycling remains within Rider.
Verify ordinary Win32, UWP, elevated, owned, cloaked, and tool windows retain current filtering.

confidence.rationale: The exact-process filter is confirmed, but Rider window topology has not yet been captured, so the grouping hypothesis remains below even odds.

issue_context.summary: Window Hopper opens for other applications but shows no sibling Rider windows when invoked from a Rider window.
known_information: Reporter tested multiple Window Hopper shortcuts on PowerToys 0.101.2362 stable.
The failure is Rider-specific; the shortcut works in other applications.
Current Window Hopper selects eligible windows whose resolved process image path matches the foreground window.
inferences: Rider may use more than one process identity or an ownership arrangement rejected by the current eligibility filter.
A local HWND/process capture is needed before choosing an application-grouping rule.
issue_context.analysis: The symptom is scoped to candidate enumeration rather than global shortcut registration because the same shortcut works elsewhere. The exact process-key comparison is the first discriminating code path to test.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue and comment through 2026-08-27T06:19:22Z.

Reviewed src/modules/AltWindowCycle/AltWindowCycle.cpp and AltWindowCycleLogic.h at commit 33e4ef46e5db77a256818a917d65103c9b7398fa; candidate selection uses resolved process paths and filters invisible, cloaked, owned, and tool windows.
Searched the upstream issue tracker for Window Hopper and Rider; no separate duplicate was found.

actions.label: Design fix
actions.note: Approve a focused fork-side design investigation; this action does not write upstream.

reproduce.title: Capture why Rider windows are excluded
prerequisites: JetBrains Rider with two projects in separate top-level windows
Window Hopper enabled with a non-conflicting shortcut
setup: Record each Rider window title and whether it belongs to the same or a different rider64.exe process.
steps: Invoke Window Hopper and record whether the overlay appears.
Use a window-inspection tool or debugger to record HWND, owner HWND, process ID/path, visibility, cloaked state, and tool-window style for both Rider frames.
Repeat with two windows from a simple Win32 app as a control.
reproduce.expected_result: Both Rider windows are eligible and displayed, or the captured identity/eligibility difference identifies the precise filter that removes them.
